newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish banks to complete fund changes by June 19.
newsitem.headline: Turkish banks to complete fund changes by June 19.

text.p: Turkish banks and brokerage houses are approaching the June 19 to complete changes in their existing mutual funds in line with a decree in December by the Capital Markets Board (CMB).
Officials said the amendments on names, types, activites, establishments and public offering of mutual funds were aimed at supplying more information to investors.
"Investors will learn which instruments are included in a fund's portfolio and will know their risk," a CMB offical told Reuters.
Bankers said the CMB gave a six-month period to fund owners for the required changes.

"We changed our funds and reported them to the CMB for the approval. Although the deadline has neared, we are still awaiting. But we began informing our customers about the changes, " Meltem Erce, fund manager at Turkey's private Finans Yatirim told Reuters.
Turkish banks at present have two types of mutual funds -- type A which consists of at least 25 percent of equities and type B which is made up of fixed-income securities.
"The type of the funds will not change but we must also tell our customers whether a fund is an equity-based fund, bond fund, gold fund or etc..." Erce said.

A fund, holding at least 51 percent of its portfolio in stocks will be named a share fund. It will be named a treasury bill and bond fund if at least 51 percent of its portfolio is invested in fixed income government paper.
The changes will also ease the establishment of funds by new sectors such as insurance firms which bankers say will buoy institutional demand for the mutual funds.
Currently, 186 mutual funds operate in Turkey with a total portfolio value of 184.5 trillion lira. The CMB gave approval last week for four new ones to be set up.
Under the new system, the founder and manager of the fund will be separated to bring a more professional approach in portfolio management.
The CMB ruling also requires some changes in pricing of the funds to protect investors.
Turkey's first mutual fund, ISFON1 which is currently the second biggest, was set up by leading commercial Turkiye Is Bankasi in 1986.
The portfolio value of Turkey's biggest fund, ISFON6 which was also set up by Is Bankasi, has reached to 45 trillion lira.
